Body: Suggestion: this branch does not currently fall back to the selected agent when the last user message has no matching agent. While the session is running, `agent` becomes undefined here and the spinner uses `theme.border`, which appears to contradict the PR behavior described above. Consider falling back to `local.agent.current()` after the lookup if the message agent is missing or no longer in the primary agent list.

This changes `readdir` semantics: symlinks that point to directories are now reported as `type: \"directory\"` instead of `\"symlink\"`. That’s an observable behavior change for consumers that need to distinguish real directories vs symlinked ones. Consider preserving `type: \"symlink\"` and adding additional metadata (e.g., `targetType` or `symlinkTargetIsDirectory`) or introducing a distinct type (e.g., `\"symlink-directory\"`) to avoid breaking callers that rely on the old meaning.

Detecting missing files via a manual `_tag === \"NotFound\"` check is brittle and couples this code to the current error shape. Prefer matching on the filesystem error type/tag via the library’s typed helpers (e.g., a tag-based catch like `Effect.catchTag(...)` if available for your error model) or using an `fs.exists(...)`/`fs.stat(...)` check before reading, so missing-file handling is robust across runtime/platform changes.

These persistence tests don’t clear `mcp-state.json` upfront, so state can leak across tests/runs and make results order-dependent (especially if tests run in parallel or reuse the same `Global.Path.state`). To make the tests deterministic, remove/initialize `mcp-state.json` at the start of each persistence test (or in a shared `beforeEach` for this suite) before performing assertions.

This changes the meaning of `DirEntry.type` by returning `\"directory\"` for entries that are *actually symlinks* pointing to directories. That can be a breaking behavioral change for callers that rely on `\"symlink\"` to avoid following links or to display them differently. Consider preserving `type: \"symlink\"` and adding separate metadata (e.g., `isSymlink: true` and/or `targetType: \"directory\" | \"file\" | \"other\"`), or introducing a distinct type value so callers can distinguish real directories from symlinked ones.

Using `Promise.all` over the full `entries` list can trigger an unbounded number of concurrent `stat` calls (one per symlink). In large directories this can cause I/O spikes and potentially hit file descriptor / resource limits. Consider limiting concurrency (e.g., a small pool/limiter) or performing the `stat` calls in a controlled batch/sequence while still returning the same result shape.

Suggestion: consider validating `state` before handling `error` or the missing-code branch. Because this loopback port is fixed, a local page or process can hit `/callback?error=...` and reject/clear `pendingOAuth` without knowing the OAuth state, which can trivially cancel the login flow. The human reviewer can decide, but keeping the state check as the gate for all callback outcomes would make this harder to trigger.

Suggestion: consider seeding these copied headers from requestInput.headers when requestInput is a Request. Right now only init headers are copied, so fetch(requestInput, { ...init, headers }) can replace existing Request headers with just Authorization/User-Agent. The human reviewer can decide, but if the SDK passes a Request carrying Content-Type or metadata headers, those headers would be dropped.

budget_limited` can never reach the budget-limit prompt here because `isGoalContinueNeeded` currently returns true only for `status === "active"`. That makes the `updatedGoal.status === "budget_limited" ? ...` branch effectively dead. Consider either (a) extending `isGoalContinueNeeded` to allow a final “wrap-up” continuation when `budget_limited` (and possibly `iteration_limit_reached`) is set, or (b) changing the prompt-loop condition to explicitly handle `budget_limited` without relying on `isGoalContinueNeeded`.

isGoalContinueNeeded`’s definition conflicts with the rest of the feature behavior: the prompt loop selects a special prompt for `budget_limited`, but this function blocks any continuation when status is not `"active"`. Align this predicate with the intended continuation states (e.g., allow `budget_limited` for exactly one wrap-up turn, or provide a separate predicate for “need wrap-up prompt” vs “need autonomous continuation”).

The `as Effect.Effect<MessageV2.WithParts>` cast erases the environment requirement (`SessionGoal.Service | Config.Service`) and can hide missing layer provisioning until runtime. Prefer to propagate the environment type through `ensureRunning` / `loop` (or widen `loop`’s env accordingly) so the compiler enforces that `SessionGoal` and `Config` are provided.

The schema and types are looser than the tool’s actual contract: `status` is `Schema.String` and then narrowed at runtime, and the update call uses `params.status as any`. Define `status` as a literal union (`Schema.Literal("complete", "blocked")` or a `Schema.Union`) and type `params.status` accordingly, so `updateStatus` can be called without `any` and without a separate `valid.includes` check.

If the intent is that goals are fully experimental/disabled by default, consider gating tool registration behind the same config/flag so models/clients don’t see or call `create_goal` / `update_goal` when the feature is off.

Two issues here: (1) `thread_id` is already a primary key, so `goalThreadIdx` is redundant in SQLite (the PK already provides an index). (2) `GoalStatus` includes `"cleared"`, but `clear` deletes the row rather than updating status, so `"cleared"` appears unused/inconsistent with the storage model. Consider removing the redundant index and either dropping `"cleared"` or implementing “cleared” as a status update instead of a delete.

If they’re intended to be consumer-visible (UI/session transcript), consider mapping them to appropriate `SessionMessage` entries or updating existing messages; otherwise, add a short comment explaining they’re intentionally no-ops to avoid confusion and “lost” events during debugging.

`formatOptions(config)` is recomputed for each element in the leader-sequence `.map(...)` (and again in the non-leader path). Hoist it into a local `const options = formatOptions(config)` and reuse it so the formatting path does less allocation/work per render, especially when formatting many bindings.

`formatKeyBindings` now returns `undefined` when `bindings` is empty/undefined, whereas it previously returned the result of `formatCommandBindingsExtra(...)` (very likely a string). This is a behavioral/API change for callers and can surface as missing labels where an empty string was previously expected. Consider returning `""` for the empty case (or explicitly typing the return as `string` and ensuring it always returns a string) to keep the function’s contract stable.

The new tests repeat a large shared setup pattern (renderer/keymap/config/register layer/get bindings/cleanup) across multiple cases, increasing the cost of future edits to keymap setup. Consider extracting a small helper (e.g., `withKeymapBindings({ scope, commands, configOverrides }, callback)` or similar) that returns the sequences/strings needed for assertions, so each test focuses on the expectation rather than duplicating harness plumbing.

Small style suggestion: this new comment introduces a non-ASCII em dash, while the style guide asks us to default to ASCII unless the file already uses Unicode. Consider replacing it with a comma or hyphen if you agree.

Suggestion: this still appears to miss config-only `google-vertex-anthropic` providers. The custom loader above only derives the REP `baseURL` from env-loaded options, and this fallback only runs when the provider id is `google-vertex`; if a user configures `google-vertex-anthropic` in `opencode.json` with `options.project` and `options.location: "eu"`/`"us"`, `createVertexAnthropic` will still see no `baseURL` and use the unresolved `{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com` form. Consider applying the same fallback for `google-vertex-anthropic` here as well, or teaching that custom loader to honor configured provider options.

The timeout fallback silently returns `Effect.void`, which can mask a real hang and continue execution without completing the scan/ask work. Consider surfacing this (e.g., log a warning, emit a diagnostic event, or fail with a domain-specific error that the caller can handle) so operators/users can understand why results may be incomplete.

The `\"5 seconds\"` timeout value is a magic constant and is duplicated in multiple places in this file. Extract it into a named constant (or reuse an existing config value) to keep escalation behavior consistent and easier to adjust.

The `SIGKILL` escalation pipeline (send + bounded await + asVoid) appears twice in this module. Consider factoring it into a small helper (e.g., `killAndWait(signal, timeout)`) to reduce duplication and prevent future divergence between the two kill paths.
Keeping inline for minimal diff — only two occurrences in the same file.

`selectedProjectStore` calls `globalSync.child(project.worktree, { bootstrap: false })`, but `child()` still creates a new child store (and its TanStack queries) when one doesn’t exist. This can trigger network requests / instance fanout just from opening the new-session project/branch picker. Prefer reading from `globalSync.existing(project.worktree)` (or only creating a child store after explicit selection/navigation) and fall back to "main" when the store isn’t already loaded.

The update pill text is hard-coded ("Update" / `Update ${version}`) while the rest of the titlebar strings use `language.t(...)`. To keep the titlebar fully localized, move these user-facing strings to i18n keys (including the versioned title) and use `language.t` here.

The picker’s search `<input>` relies on `placeholder` only and has no associated `<label>` or `aria-label`. For screen reader users, add an explicit accessible name (e.g., `aria-label` using the same translated string as the placeholder) so the control is announced correctly.

Suggestion: this fallback keeps the default home prompt capped at the old 75 columns, so the prompt only becomes responsive after users explicitly set `prompt.max_width` to `"auto"`. If the intended default is the PR description’s responsive behavior while preserving the small-terminal minimum, consider using the same responsive calculation when `configured` is undefined.

Either make the redirect URI use `127.0.0.1` too, or keep the listener hostless so it accepts the `localhost` resolution.

why do we have to handle the case of merging projects? can we make this simpler by running all of this in an `immediate` transaction to make sure nobody else is writing to it, and assume that we atomically migrate over an old project, and there can never be both and old and new project at the same time?

what happens when a user runs an old opencode version in the same project? is that why we are wanting to support this, so the old project can be created again and we will merge them? but that means we'd overwrite a bunch of the older fields in the new project, so we probably don't want that. if we can make it atomic & assume once it's migrated we don't touch it again, in the case when both exist (because old and new versions of opencode ran) we just ignore the old one

Kept this as `&&` intentionally. `id === global && vcs` is the no-commit/no-remote Git repo case: it still needs the opened repo directory and `vcs: git` behavior. Only non-Git global falls back to `/`, which restores the config/global behavior.

Agreed on not merging project metadata. Updated migration to run in an immediate transaction and only copy the old project row when the new row does not exist. If both old and new rows exist, the new project row stays authoritative; references are moved and the old project row is deleted. I left permission merging because otherwise we can drop allow/deny rules keyed to one of the IDs.

`childVersion` is incremented on child store creation only. Callers use this signal to recompute views based on `existing()` children, but when a child store is evicted/disposed the signal will not change, so UIs can keep rendering stale sessions/metadata. Consider also bumping `childVersion` from the child manager `onDispose` hook (or providing a reactive children map) so consumers are notified on removals as well as additions.

`enrich()` reads `globalSync.existing()` but does not have any reactive dependency that changes when a child store becomes available. As a result, the project list may never pick up per-workspace persisted icon overrides after the workspace loads (unless some unrelated reactive change re-triggers `enriched()`). If the intent is “use child metadata only after loaded”, wire this memo/effect to a reactive version signal (e.g. `globalSync.childVersion()`) or expose a reactive children list.

`records` recomputation is forced via `sync.childVersion()`, but that version currently only updates on child creation. If the child store manager evicts/disposes a workspace store, `records()` may keep returning sessions from the disposed store indefinitely. Ensure the version signal also changes on dispose/eviction (or otherwise track removals) so `records` drops sessions for removed stores.

The query key includes all `projectDirectories()` (root + sandboxes), but the query function only loads sessions for the root directory. This can create multiple distinct cache entries and trigger redundant refetches when the sandbox list changes, even though the side effect is identical. Consider using a query key derived from just the root (and optionally `enabled: !!root`) to keep caching/refetch behavior consistent with what’s loaded.

Suggestion only, human can decide: this currently misses a bold title when the reasoning stream contains only the title so far, because the regex requires the blank-line separator. In hide mode that leaves the collapsed header as just "Thinking" until more content arrives, and a title-only summary would never surface its title. Consider allowing end-of-string as a valid title boundary while still requiring either the blank-line separator or EOF to avoid matching ordinary leading bold text.

Suggestion for the human reviewer: the docs above say explicit include wins over includeEncryptedReasoning, but if include is present and filters to an empty array, this falls through to the alias. That makes { include: [], includeEncryptedReasoning: true } still send reasoning.encrypted_content. Consider returning undefined as soon as an explicit include array is provided, after filtering invalid entries.

Suggestion for the human reviewer: this only forwards an include value when the caller explicitly set include/includeEncryptedReasoning. Direct @opencode-ai/llm OpenAI models still default GPT-5 Responses requests to store:false with reasoningSummary:auto, so those stateless reasoning calls will not request reasoning.encrypted_content unless every caller opts in. Consider deriving include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"] here when store === false and reasoning is enabled, unless an explicit include was provided.

Suggestion (optional): this final `trim()` can strip markdown-significant leading spaces from the extracted body. For example, `**Title**\n\n    code` would render as plain text instead of an indented code block after extraction. Since the separator blank lines are already consumed by the regex, consider preserving leading body whitespace and only trimming the end here.

The updated `same` logic becomes `true` whenever `ag.model` is unset, which can cause `ag.variant` to be auto-applied even when `input.model` explicitly overrides the model. That changes behavior beyond 'inherited/default model' cases and can inadvertently apply a variant to an explicitly chosen model/provider. Consider making `same` sensitive to whether `input.model` was provided (e.g., only treat it as `same` when the model is inherited/default, or when an explicit `input.model` matches `ag.model` if configured).

Typing `assistantModel` as `typeof ref` tightly couples this helper to the exact shape of the test fixture. To keep the helper stable if `ref` changes, consider narrowing the option type to only the fields used here (e.g., `{ providerID: ..., modelID: ... }`), or reuse the project’s model identifier type if one exists.

Forwarding a proxy URL from an environment variable without validation can enable traffic interception/data exfiltration if `ADAL_APP_URL` is set unexpectedly (e.g., via user shell/environment injection). Consider validating the value before passing it to the sidecar (e.g., parse as URL; enforce `https` scheme; optionally restrict hosts to an allowlist or only enable in explicitly configured/dev modes) so the sidecar won’t silently route sensitive LLM traffic to an arbitrary endpoint.

Using `std::env::var` forces UTF-8 and will drop non-UTF8 environment values; for env pass-through, `std::env::var_os` is typically more robust. If the sidecar expects a URL string specifically, consider parsing/validating and then re-serializing to a known-good UTF-8 string; otherwise prefer `var_os` + `Command::env_os` (or equivalent) to preserve the original value.

✅ **Addressed in force-push.** Now validates that only localhost/loopback URLs are accepted:

```rust
if url_str.starts_with("http://localhost")
    || url_str.starts_with("http://127.0.0.1")
    || url_str.starts_with("http://[::1]")
```

Non-local URLs are rejected with `tracing::warn`. This prevents any env injection from routing sensitive traffic externally.

HTTPS enforcement was considered but intentionally omitted — localhost proxies typically run plain HTTP (TLS adds complexity for loopback with no security benefit since traffic never leaves the machine).

The JSONC fixture here likely isn’t invalid: JSONC commonly allows comments and trailing commas, so this test may pass even if the parser is strict about “invalid JSONC”. To make the test reliably exercise the “invalid JSONC” path, use a truly invalid construct (e.g., unterminated string/object, stray comma, malformed comment) and assert the fallback behavior.

Returning `{ } as Info` is an unsafe type assertion that can violate invariants expected by downstream code (it bypasses schema/defaulting guarantees). Prefer returning a real empty/default `Info` value produced by the same schema/constructor path used elsewhere (e.g., a dedicated “default config” value/function), so required fields and defaults are consistently applied without relying on a cast.

The `catchCause` now covers more than “invalid JSON/schema” (it also swallows failures from plugin resolution and schema write-back). This can mask actionable operational errors (e.g., a plugin path typo) and silently fall back to defaults. Consider narrowing the catch to only parsing/schema-validation failures, while allowing plugin resolution errors (and potentially unexpected IO errors) to surface to the caller.

This test name implies schema validation is handled gracefully, but the assertion (`username` is defined) doesn’t verify that the invalid field was actually detected/ignored or that fallback behavior occurred for the right reason. Strengthen the assertion to validate the intended behavior directly (e.g., confirm the invalid field isn’t present in the resolved config and/or that the config equals the known defaults for this scenario).
Fixed — changed fixture to unterminated JSONC (trailing comma at last property, missing closing brace). 85ed2e482
Fixed — replaced `{} as Info` with `Schema.decodeSync(Info)({})` which produces a properly typed empty config through the schema. 85ed2e482

Addressed two ways: (1) parse/schema lines are the only ones in the narrow `catchCause` (sync-throw defect risk); (2) plugin resolution now has its own `catchCause` that logs the error but returns the parsed config (sans plugins) — so a plugin typo in one file doesn't collapse all global config loading. 109a6eb48
Fixed — added `expect("invalid_field" in config).toBe(false)` to verify the invalid field is absent in the resolved config. 85ed2e482

Schema.decodeSync(Info)({})` can itself throw if `Info` has required fields without defaults, which would defeat the goal of “handling invalid config gracefully without crashing” (the catch-handler would fail). To make the fallback reliably non-throwing, use a non-throwing decode (e.g., decode-to-Either/Option) or a known-safe explicit default value for `Info` (and optionally log if even the fallback cannot be constructed).

This changes behavior from “fail config load if plugin resolution fails” to “log and continue”. If downstream code assumes plugins are resolved (or relies on failures to surface misconfiguration), continuing with partially-resolved/unstyled plugin specs can lead to hard-to-diagnose runtime behavior. Consider either (a) rethrowing after logging (preserve prior semantics) or (b) returning a structured warning/diagnostic that callers can surface, so failure isn’t silent while still avoiding a hard crash.

The assertion `expect(config.username).toBeDefined()` is likely too weak to validate the intended behavior, because it can pass even if the loader always returns a default config regardless of input. To make this test meaningfully detect regressions, assert a specific expected value/source (e.g., that known-good fields from the file are preserved when schema is mostly valid, or that a known default value is returned when validation fails), rather than only checking “defined”.

`singleStatus` references `requireSession` before `requireSession` is declared. While this will typically work at runtime due to closures, it commonly trips `no-use-before-define` linting and makes the flow harder to read. Prefer moving `requireSession` above `singleStatus` (or inlining the check) so dependencies are declared before use.

`singleStatus` appears to do two sequential lookups/validations for the same `sessionID` (`requireSession(...)` and then `statusSvc.get(...)`). If `requireSession` hits storage and `statusSvc.get` also hits storage, this will add avoidable latency and load. Consider collapsing this into a single call path (e.g., rely on `statusSvc.get` to validate session existence and map not-found to the same API error, or add a `statusSvc.getOrFailSessionNotFound(sessionID)`-style helper) so the endpoint only incurs one backend read.

The endpoint name `singleStatus` is a bit awkward as a public API surface (it reads like an implementation detail and can be inconsistent with typical resource naming). A clearer convention is usually `getStatus` / `statusById` / `statusForSession`, while keeping the path `/session/:sessionID/status` as-is. Renaming the endpoint key also improves generated clients (method names) and documentation readability.

`getStatus` performs (at least) two separate lookups: one via `requireSession(sessionID)` and another via `statusSvc.get(sessionID)`. If `statusSvc.get` already validates existence / maps not-found appropriately, consider removing the extra `requireSession` call to avoid redundant storage reads. If `requireSession` is needed for error shaping, consider folding that logic into `statusSvc.get` (or providing a `statusSvc.getOrNotFound` variant) so the endpoint only hits storage once.

The `SessionPaths` key name `singleStatus` is inconsistent with the endpoint/handler name `getStatus`. To keep the API surface easier to navigate (especially as routes grow), consider renaming the path key to match the endpoint name (e.g., `getStatus`) or to a clearly paired convention with the existing `status` path (e.g., `statusById`).

The `SessionPaths` key name `singleStatus` is inconsistent with the endpoint/handler name `getStatus`. To keep the API surface easier to navigate (especially as routes grow), consider renaming the path key to match the endpoint name (e.g., `getStatus`) or to a clearly paired convention with the existing `status` path (e.g., `statusById`).

This handler performs two lookups for the same `sessionID` (`requireSession(...)` and then `statusSvc.get(...)`). If both hit storage, this adds avoidable latency and load. Consider collapsing this into a single read (e.g., have `statusSvc.get` be responsible for producing the same not-found error mapping as `requireSession`, or refactor to reuse the value returned by `requireSession` if it already contains what `statusSvc.get` needs).

Keeping requireSession intentionally. statusSvc.get() reads from an in-memory Map (via InstanceState.get) and always returns { type: "idle" } for any unknown sessionID — it never fails. Removing requireSession would cause this endpoint to return 200 idle for completely non-existent sessions instead of a proper 404. The two calls serve different purposes: requireSession validates session existence against storage, statusSvc.get reads runtime status from memory.
Addressed in latest commits: replaced Schema.decodeSync(Info)({}) with {} as Info. Since all Info fields are Schema.optional, an empty object satisfies the type without risk of throwing.

Addressed in latest commits: kept the catchCause (graceful startup is the PR's goal) but now logs with Cause.pretty(cause) for safe structured diagnostics. Plugin resolution errors are logged at ERROR level with full context but don't crash startup.

Addressed in latest commits: test now writes a valid model field alongside the invalid one and asserts config.model === "test/model". This proves the config system correctly preserves valid fields while rejecting invalid ones.

Returning `{}` for *any* schema validation failure discards otherwise-valid fields from the file. This conflicts with the updated test expectation that valid keys (e.g., `model`) are retained while unknown keys are ignored. Consider splitting the error handling so that JSON/JSONC parse errors skip the file, but schema errors preserve the parsed object where possible (e.g., validate in a “strip unknown keys” mode, or explicitly filter out unknown keys and keep the rest) rather than dropping the entire config to `{}`.

`Cause.pretty(cause)` may include raw parse error details that can embed snippets of the config content (potentially including secrets like tokens). Consider logging a redacted/summarized error (e.g., error type + location) and avoid emitting the full pretty-printed cause at error level, or ensure sensitive values are scrubbed before logging.

`resolveLoadedPlugins` mutates `config.plugin` entries in-place; if it throws partway through, catching at the outer promise level can leave `data.plugin` in a partially-resolved/partially-original state, which is hard to reason about operationally. Prefer resolving into a new array (or resolving each entry with per-item error handling and leaving the original spec intact on failure), and consider surfacing a structured warning to the user that plugins were not loaded rather than silently continuing with possibly inconsistent plugin specs.

The new behavior includes a dedicated catch path for plugin-resolution failures (`"plugin resolution failed"`) and a catch path for schema validation failures. There isn’t a test exercising either: (1) a config with `plugin` entries that trigger a resolution error, verifying load succeeds and the plugin list is left in a consistent state; and (2) a schema-invalid-but-parseable config verifying the intended “keep valid keys, drop invalid keys” behavior. Adding targeted tests would guard against regressions in these new fallback behaviors.

Fixed: added stripUnknownKeys() helper that filters parsed data to only include known Info fields before calling ConfigParse.schema. Unknown keys are silently dropped, valid fields are preserved. Schema validation now only rejects genuinely invalid structure, not unrecognized keys.

Fixed: removed cause from all log.error calls. ConfigParse.jsonc embeds the full expanded config text in JsonError messages, so even Cause.pretty leaked it. Now logs only the file path with a static message.
Fixed: resolveLoadedPlugins now wraps each iteration in try/catch, logging per-plugin failures and preserving the original spec. Partial mutation on thrown-to-completion is no longer possible.

Fixed: added test 'handles plugin resolution failure gracefully' that loads a config with a non-existent plugin path and asserts model is preserved. The existing test 'handles invalid schema gracefully without crashing' already exercises the schema-invalid-but-parseable case (asserts model retention).

`cause.reasons` / `Cause.isDieReason` is likely not a valid way to introspect an Effect Cause (and will either fail at runtime or omit relevant non-defect failures like schema validation errors). Prefer using Effect/Cause utilities that are known to exist for extracting defects/failures (e.g., logging `Cause.pretty(cause)` and/or using `Cause.squash(cause)` / `Cause.defects(cause)`), so the handler can’t crash and provides actionable error details for both parse and schema failures.

Returning `{} as Info` bypasses schema validation/defaulting guarantees and can produce a value that does not actually satisfy `Info` at runtime (risking downstream runtime errors when required fields are accessed). Instead, return a schema-produced empty/default config (e.g., decode an empty object via the schema so defaults apply), or return a well-defined safe fallback value that truly conforms to `Info`.

`known` is recomputed on every call, even though it’s derived from a static schema. Consider hoisting the computed set to a module-level constant so repeated config loads (and multi-file merges) don’t repeatedly allocate/compute the same set.

This test’s goal is “doesn’t crash”, but it asserts `config.username` is defined, which can be brittle if defaults/environment change. A more direct and stable assertion is to check the effect succeeds (e.g., assert `Exit.isSuccess(yield* Config.use.get().pipe(Effect.exit))`), and only assert specific fields when they are explicitly provided by the test inputs.

The test goal is proving doesnot crash — the name says gracefully without crashing. toBeDefined() on any field proves the Effect succeeded without failing, which is exactly the behavior under test. An Exit.isSuccess assertion would work too but provides the same signal.

Suggestion: this rejects mixed variants within a single parsed file, but config files are parsed before they are merged. A global config with `tool_output: { truncate: false }` plus a project config with `tool_output: { max_lines: 200 }` can still merge into the invalid combined shape, and `limits()` will silently disable truncation because `truncate === false`. Consider revalidating the merged config or normalizing `tool_output` during merge so the public “cannot be combined” rule applies across config layers too.
